subject: Intermittent regional throttling — request to validate SLA credit eligibility
messages:
From: Nadia Ortiz <support@gleampay.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected 429/503 spike in us-west-2 on Aug 9

Hi Priyom,

We observed an intermittent spike of 429 and 503 responses for several of our production routes between ~08:45–09:15 PDT (us-west-2). Rough numbers: ~40% of requests for our high-volume key routes returned 429/503, with error bursts every 30–90s. We attached a small sample of traces and a short timeline extract.

Can you confirm whether this maps to a Redwood-side throttling / regional issue and whether this qualifies for SLA credit under our contract (DL-8492)? We need the official downtime window and any supporting evidence to open a billing claim.

Attachments: customer-trace-20270809.txt

Thanks,
Nadia Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability
GleamPay

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Ortiz <support@gleampay.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429/503 spike in us-west-2 on Aug 9

Hi Nadia — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the traces. We’re reviewing this now. Quick asks to help us triage:

- Can you confirm precise start/end timestamps in UTC for the most impacted traces?
- Approx requests/sec and percent of traffic affected for those routes (rough numbers are fine).
- Any indication this coincided with a customer-side deploy or rate-limit changes?

Immediate next steps on our side: I’ve looped in Ben and Monica from account and escalation. We’ll pull SLO snapshots and region metrics and come back with a verified downtime window and evidence log. If it’s our side, we’ll trigger the credit process and produce an RCA.

I’ll follow up within 45 minutes with a preliminary window.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: (internal) GleamPay — validate regional metrics and SLO snapshot

Evelyn — can you pull availability and 5xx/4xx error rate for us-west-2 and the following routes for 08:30–09:30 PDT (UTC 15:30–16:30)? Customer reports bursty 429/503s and wants a verified downtime window and SLO evidence.

Routes (from customer): /api/v1/payments, /api/v1/charges, /stream/connect

Please attach:
- Aggregated 1m/5m error rate and availability
- Request counts (RPS) for the window
- Any autoscaler or capacity events, instance restarts, or throttling logs
- SLO snapshot (availability) for the billing period and a short note on whether the observed window would cross their SLA threshold for credit.

I’ve attached the customer trace for context.

Attachments: customer-trace-20270809.txt

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (internal) GleamPay — validate regional metrics and SLO snapshot

Folks — quick summary from infra side after correlating metrics and control-plane events:

- Verified increased 429/503 error rate in us-west-2 between 2027-08-09T08:44:00Z and 2027-08-09T09:12:30Z (UTC).
- Peak error rate: ~42% aggregated across the three listed routes. Total affected RPS ~2.2k (down from normal ~5.5k for those routes).
- Cause: an autoscaler regression that delayed pod scale-up during a short traffic surge; resulting token-bucket throttles on the request path until new capacity came online. Root cause flagged in control plane autoscaler v2.1.3 rollout.
- Evidence attached: slo-snapshot-20270809.csv (availability and request counts), control-plane event log snippets, and a draft RCA (rca-draft-20270809.md).

Per contract DL-8492 SLA (availability 99.5% monthly), the observed window pushes the monthly availability for the customer below the threshold for partial credit. I recommend we proceed with credit calculation and a public-facing postmortem.

Next steps:
- I'll finalize the RCA and an evidence bundle for billing.
- Prio: open billing ticket and calculate prorated credit amount (estimated).
- Marissa / Monica — please coordinate customer communications cadence.

Attachments: slo-snapshot-20270809.csv, rca-draft-20270809.md

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Ortiz <support@gleampay.com>, Billing Team <billing@gleampay.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429/503 spike in us-west-2 on Aug 9 — verification and next steps

Hi Nadia — thanks again for the traces and patience. Internal validation is complete: we verified an elevated 429/503 error rate in us-west-2 between 2027-08-09T08:44:00Z and 2027-08-09T09:12:30Z (UTC). The root cause was an autoscaler regression during a rollout which delayed capacity scaling, causing transient throttling.

Per our review, this event reduces the monthly availability below the SLA threshold in DL-8492, so the account is eligible for a prorated credit. What we’re doing next:

- Evelyn is finalizing the RCA and preparing the evidence bundle (attached draft).
- Billing has been cc’d and will open a credit ticket (BILL-5721). Expect an email from billing with the credit calculation within 3 business days.
- We’ll publish a customer-facing postmortem summary within 5 business days; I’ll share the link as soon as it’s ready.

If you’d like an immediate call to walk through the RCA and calculation, I can set up a 30-min slot today.

Attachments: rca-draft-20270809.md, slo-snapshot-20270809.csv

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll share the full postmortem and remediation steps shortly.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
